description: Fire an agent whenever a record reaches a given state (or, with relation_field instead of a state, whenever a record's relation field is linked to the agent). By default it starts the agent by itself, so it fits an agent meant to run on its own. A run is not held for approval as a whole: outward actions its writes set off (email, Slack, webhook, HTTP, social post) are staged for a person, with one exception: a send_email whose recipients (to and cc) are all active workspace members runs as configured unless the agent's approval_policy lists email. human_gate:true means it NEVER fires by itself (a person starts each run). The state field must be a select/workflow and the option one of its own (describe_database shows them). [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES create_agent_trigger"]

agent.description: The agent record's uuid or public number.

database.description: The database whose state changes should fire the agent.

human_gate.description: true = "ask me before each run": this trigger never starts a run by itself; a person starts each run (ADR-0010). The default is false: the agent wakes by itself. Not the same as holding the agent's writes for approval.

relation_field.description: Relation binding (instead of state_field + state): a relation field on the database that points at the Agents database, e.g. "Next". Linking it to the agent wakes the agent (#1130).

state.description: State binding: the option that fires it — the human label, e.g. "New".

state_field.description: State binding: the select/workflow field to watch (name, api_name, or id).
